results.title: C2ME: Characterizing Ciphertext Matrix Multiplication Encodings for FHE Inference
results.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Workload Characterization
results.abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation directly on encrypted data, making it a promising approach for privacy-preserving neural network inference. Ciphertext-ciphertext matrix multiplication (CC-MM) is a recurring kernel in encrypted Transformer attention and a major contributor to end-to-end latency. Prior work has proposed several encoding strategies for CKKS-based CC-MM: row-based, diagonal-based (THOR), column-based (MOAI), and bicyclic (BMM-I, BMM-III). Each has been evaluated under different FHE parameters, software libraries, hardware platforms, and metrics, making direct comparison difficult.This paper presents a systematic characterization of these four encodings under a unified Lattigo and a Cheddar GPU implementation, evaluating operation counts, evaluation-key memory, runtime, peak working-set memory, and energy across square matrices of dimension 128 to 2048. Analyzing this data, we present encoding-specific opportunities to reuse hoisted key-switching state and plaintext masks at different granularities in BMM-I and BMM-III, exposing tunable runtime-memory tradeoffs. Our results show that operation counts alone do not predict practical performance: local (intra-block) hoisting improves BMM-I runtime by up to 2.3× without changing rotation counts, while broader cross-block reuse reduces rotations and key-switches by up to 23× but yields only 6.2× runtime improvement using substantially more peak memory. The best encoding depends on the deployment objective. MOAI provides the highest batched throughput through SIMD slot utilization, BMM-I with intra-block hoisting minimizes peak working-set memory, and BMM-III blocked hoisting provides a balanced runtime-memory tradeoff on CPU. Additional experiments across CKKS polynomial degrees and an NVIDIA H100 show that the latency-optimal encoding can shift with matrix dimension, parameterization, and hardware, while the broader runtime-memory-throughput tradeoff remains. We therefore argue that encrypted CC-MM encodings should be selected according to deployment constraints rather than homomorphic operation counts alone.
